verdicts.title: Planetarium view hotkeys swallow typing in the search field - object search by name is unusable from the keyboard
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly, twice, on a fresh v-planetarium profile (site 40.00N/105.00W). Plan Tonight > Planetarium > sidebar toggle > click 'Search objects, names...' > type 'Vega' left literally 'Va' in the field, and the RA/Dec grid (labels +30/+15/0/-15, 3h..23h) plus the yellow ecliptic line both switched on behind the panel (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vp-09.png = before, vp-10.png = after). Clearing and typing 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' left exactly 'abd' (vp-12.png), matching the reported string character for character. Code path confirms it: planetarium_screen.dart:259-262 wraps the whole screen in Focus(autofocus:true, onKeyEvent:_handleKeyEvent), and _handleKeyEvent (actions.dart:507) returns KeyEventResult.handled for bare keyH/keyR/keyG/keyC/keyE/keyN/keyM/keyF with no check for whether the primary focus is a text input, so the ancestor Focus consumes the KeyEvent that the TextField's own IME path never sees as text.

verdicts.title: Object info popup keeps the old object's name and coordinates but recomputes Alt/Az for the NEW selection - it said Deneb was 'Below Horizon' while Deneb was 11.5 deg up
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with a different pair of objects and checked against my own alt/az computation, not the app's. Site 40.00N/105.00W. Clicked a star on the chart: popup opened for HIP24951 (mag 6.5, Star A2V+, RA 5h20m39.2s, Dec +46d57'49"), Current Position 81.2 deg / Az 325.0 deg, badge 'Daylight' (shot vp-15.png). Without closing it I typed '6720' in the panel search and clicked the M57 result (vp-16.png at 2026-08-02 16:05:25 UTC): the view recentred on RA 18h53m35s Dec +33d01' and the selection ring moved to M57, the popup still read HIP24951 / mag 6.5 / A2V+ / RA 5h20m39.2s / Dec +46d57'49", and its Current Position flipped to -15.5 deg, Az 346.2 deg with a red 'Below Horizon' badge. My independent computation (GMST->LST, spherical transform, no app code) for 2026-08-02 16:05:25 UTC at 40N/105W: HIP24951 alt +81.19 az 324.67; M57 alt -15.54 az 346.31. LST check 5h50.5m vs the app footer's 05:50. So the popup is showing M57's horizon position and M57's 'Below Horizon' warning under HIP24951's name and catalogue coordinates, agreeing with M57 to 0.1 deg while the named star is 81 deg up. Mechanism confirmed in code: object_info_popup.dart:476 `final altAz = ref.watch(selectedObjectAltAzProvider)!` reads the GLOBAL selection, while name/mag/type/RA/Dec come from `widget.object`, which planetarium_shell.dart:303-306 feeds from the shell's local `_popupObject` (actions.dart:100-103) - a field only written on a sky tap and never resynced when the selection changes from search. Same divergence at object_info_popup.dart:232 (observability chip) and :642. SECOND independent instant, in the opposite direction: with the same stale popup open I pressed TONIGHT (time jumped to 2026-08-03 00:00:03 local = 04:00:03 UTC). The popup, still headed HIP24951, then read Alt 75.0 deg / Az 112.4 deg with a GREEN 'Excellent' badge (shot vp-17.png). My computation for that instant at 40N/105W: M57 alt 75.0 az 112.4; HIP24951 alt -2.8 az 4.5. So the app badged a star that is 2.8 deg BELOW the horizon as an excellent target, again matching the other object to 0.1 deg. The defect therefore lies in both directions and survives a time change, ruling out any transient/one-frame explanation.
verdicts.location_wrong: Symptom and file are right, but the finding does not name the second half of the defect: the stale value lives in the SHELL, not the popup. object_info_popup.dart:476 is the read site; the field that goes stale is `_popupObject` in planetarium_screen.dart:101, set only in actions.dart:100-103 and cleared in _dismissPopup (actions.dart:110-116), and passed to the popup at widgets/redesign/planetarium_shell.dart:303-306. A fixer who only touches object_info_popup.dart can make the alt/az agree with the header but will still leave a popup describing an object that is no longer selected. Also correcting one sub-claim: the finding says the Slew button targets a different object than the popup describes; it does not. _handleSlewToTarget/_sendToFraming/_addToSequencer/_addPopupObjectToTargetQueue all use `_popupObject` (actions.dart:141, 243, 266, 320, 327), so every action button acts on the object NAMED in the popup. Only the Current Position row and the observability badge come from the other object.

verdicts.title: At a 1-degree imaging FOV the sky renders essentially empty - measured 1 star in 0.6 sq deg at astronomical dark
verdicts.reasoning: Symptom reproduced and the cause independently proved from the shipped catalog binary, not from the app. Drove Plan Tonight > Planetarium at site 40N/105W, pressed TONIGHT (time became 2026-08-03 00:00, astro dusk), scroll-zoomed to FOV 1.2 deg short axis centred on M57 (RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33d01'). The sky canvas (2.271 x 1.200 deg = 2.725 sq deg) contained 12 star blobs by an 8-connected >=3px detector on the raw capture (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vp-24.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vp-25.png) = 4.4 stars/sq deg. I then decoded the bundled pack myself: apps/desktop/assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1/tiles, 768 NSPLNT01 tiles (64-byte header + 16*lod_levels LOD index + 28-byte records of {u32 id, u32 flags, f32 x,y,z unit vector, f32 mag, f32 B-V}; validated by recovering HIP 14135 = Menkar at RA 3h02m Dec +4.09 mag 2.54). Total 119,432 stars = 2.90/sq deg whole-sky, and the count saturates at mag ~10 (N<=9 is 83,479; N<=12 is 117,930; N<=15 is 119,432) - i.e. complete only to about mag 9, exactly as the finding says. In the exact rendered footprint the pack holds 13 stars, faintest mag 9.0, and NOTHING fainter than 9.0 exists there at any magnitude. So the app is drawing 12 of the 13 stars it owns: the render is not dropping anything, the catalog is empty. A real Lyra field (galactic latitude ~+13) has of order 100-200 stars/sq deg to mag 12, so the chart is roughly 30x too shallow at imaging scale. There is also no escape hatch in a shipped build: the deep-star tier (deep_star_providers.dart) is off by default, only engages below 8 deg, and layers_panel.dart:415-419 documents that no tileset is published - deep_star_catalog_card.dart:250 asks the user for their OWN 'https://your-host/skotiq_deep_stars' base URL. Out of the box mag ~9 is a hard ceiling.
verdicts.location_wrong: Yes - the cited where is the wrong file to hand a fixer. render_config.dart:434-489 is dynamicMagnitudeLimitsProvider and it does contain the FOV ramp, but that code is working: at FOV 1.2 at astro dark it reaches its 12.0 clamp, and the pack has zero stars between mag 9.0 and 12.0 anywhere in this field, so editing the ramp changes nothing on screen. The finding's own 'expected' says as much, yet the where points there anyway. The actionable sites are (a) the bundled pack's depth (apps/desktop/assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1 + the build_hyg_tiles source), (b) the deep-star tier that is off-by-default and has no published tileset: deep_star_providers.dart (showDeepStarsProvider default false, kDeepStarFovThresholdDegrees 8.0, kHygFaintFloorMag 11.5), layers_panel.dart:413-460, deep_star_catalog_card.dart, and (c) the missing user-facing signal - star_catalog_fallback_banner.dart fires only when HYG is absent entirely, never when HYG's mag-9 floor is what is emptying the field. Also correcting one number: the headline '1 star in 0.6 sq deg' is an unlucky patch, not the typical case. Whole-sky the pack is 2.90 stars/sq deg and I measured 4.4/sq deg in a 2.7 sq deg field; 1 in 0.6 sq deg is Poisson noise around that mean. The defect is real at ~3-5 stars/sq deg; quoting 1 overstates it by a factor of a few.
